title: High-level waste transportation capacity
bottleneck: Moving spent fuel to any future repository, or between sites, requires certified transport casks, specialized railcars, and trained crews, none of which exist at the scale a repository program needs. The US has conducted a few thousand safe shipments, but a repository would need tens of thousands over decades. Cask manufacturing capacity, route approvals, and state-level opposition are all unresolved.
why_it_blocks: A repository without transportation is a hole in the ground. Waste stranded at more than 70 sites cannot reach centralized storage or disposal without a transport system that takes a decade to build. State and tribal opposition to transport routes can block shipments for years even after federal certification.
current_state: Existing cask designs are certified and shipments have an excellent safety record. Fleet-scale transport infrastructure has not been built.
